'''Robert Geroch''' (born 1 June 1942 in [[Akron, Ohio]])<ref>''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale, 2004</ref> is an American [[theoretical physicist]] and professor at the [[University of Chicago]]. He has worked prominently on [[general relativity]] and [[mathematical physics]] and has promoted the use of [[category theory]] in mathematics and physics. He was the [[Ph.D.]] supervisor for [[Abhay Ashtekar]], [[Basilis C. Xanthopoulos|Basilis Xanthopoulos]] and [[Gary Horowitz]]. ==Education==
Geroch obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree from [[Princeton University]] in 1967 under the supervision of [[John Archibald Wheeler]], with a thesis on ''Singularities in the spacetime of general relativity: their definition, existence, and local characterization''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=92456}}</ref>
